numbering: life/examples steps are zero-based steps[n], matching apply-rulings.ts; outline frame is act 0 and numbered acts retain their numbers

rulings.barItem: content must bear out the step name; vendor-backed client request facts
rulings.finding: The story attributes these calls to Twenty through its pinned SDK. Twenty passes an ArrayBuffer to files.write. In e2b 2.45.0 that nonstreamable input uses multipart by default, not the octet-stream body in step 15. files.list also sends depth:1, omitted in step 17. The named fake fixtures should recognize these actual requests.
rulings.source: ~/.cache/twin-demand/twentyhq__twenty/packages/twenty-server/src/engine/core-modules/code-interpreter/drivers/e2b.driver.ts:124; https://registry.npmjs.org/e2b/-/e2b-2.45.0.tgz, Filesystem.write at dist/index.mjs:1853-1907 and Filesystem.list at 1942-1951
rulings.requiredChanges: Step 15 must send a real multipart body containing the unchanged 2 newline 3 newline bytes, with its file field filename /home/user/values.txt, the path query unchanged and content-type naming its boundary. Step 17 must add depth:1 to its JSON request. In step 1 update only the matching upload/list fixture requestText strings to the new requests; preserve the configured replies and all other fixtures.

rulings.barItem: content must bear out the step name
rulings.finding: Twenty connects with only {apiKey}; the pinned SDK therefore sends the default 300-second connect timeout. The current 120-second connect body is not that request. Its following setTimeout(120) is the operation that resets the exact idle deadline.
rulings.requiredChanges: Change step 21 body.timeout to 300 and make its name explicit that SDK connect resumes with its five-minute default. Keep the following exact setTimeout(120) step unchanged.

rulings.barItem: vendor behaviour contradicted; a run of refusals and same cause drawn twice
rulings.finding: RH2 always creates its task with timeout 3600, so its claimed default expiry at 20 seconds cannot occur. Steps 35 and 36 also make two consecutive failures from that one expiry.
rulings.source: ~/.cache/twin-demand/volter-ai__runhuman-2/bots/runhuman-model/machine.ts:15-20,53-56; architecture What a judge rejects first bullet
rulings.requiredChanges: Step 33 must identify a later RH2 task whose launcher is pending and send timeout 3600 (retain its template and captured identifiers; include the task environment if modeling the full RH2 request). Step 34 must wait 65m and show the launcher stalled beyond the one-hour budget and the run abandoned. Delete original step 35 instead of submitting a second expired-process refusal. Original step 36 remains the one justified already-gone cleanup response.

doubts.doubt: The vendored September 2026 spec marks the legacy connect endpoint deprecated, but the exact pinned e2b 2.45.0 SDK still calls it and supplies no shutdown date; the journey clock defaults to January 2026. I cannot establish a deprecation before that date and therefore do not issue a wrong-era ruling.
